sentences.text: 4. Mr. Sambhaji Kharatmol, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the National Highway Authority of India in some of these matters, has tendered an affidavit-in-reply.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: He has contended that these Petitions should not be entertained because all the Petitioners have an alternate remedy under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 ("Arbitration Act").
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Further, the affidavit states that if the Petitioners are affected by non- payment of solatium and interest in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Tarsem Singh (Supra), 'petitioner should promptly file claims with the Competent Authority, including all necessary documentation and prove that, (2019) 9 SCC 304 903-WP.9608.2023 & 904.WP.11052.2024.DOCX he is entitled for solatium and interest, but the Petitioner without availing the remedy directly approached this Hon'ble Court by way of writ petition, which is against the settled position of law, hence, the Writ Petition filed by the Petitioner deserves to be dismissed holding that the same is not maintainable.'
5.

sentences.text: 6. Therefore, the Petitioners preferred petitions under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: A common judgment and order dated 4 May 2023 disposed of these.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: In this judgment and order, the Principal District Judge, Nashik, [PDJ], in fact agreed with the Petitioner's contention that they were entitled to solatium and interest in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Tarsem Singh (supra).
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: This judgment and order records that even the National Highway Authority expressed willingness to pay the solatium component from the decision date in Tarsem Singh (supra).
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
However, the PDJ, being bound by the decision of the Co- ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Rishabhkumar Vs Secretary to Government of India2, felt disabled to modify the Arbitrator's award and grant the Petitioners relief in terms of the 2021 SCC OnLine Bom 4561 903-WP.9608.2023 &
904.WP.11052.2024.DOCX decision of the Hon'ble Supreme court in the case of Tarsem Singh (supra).
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The above is evident from paragraphs 25 to 26 of the PDJ's order disposing of the Petitioner's Petitions under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Paragraphs 25 and 26 are transcribed below for the convenience of reference: -
"25.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: I do agree with the submissions made by learned Advocate Mr. S.N.Baste appearing for the applicants that applicants are entitled for solatium and interest on solatium.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: So also National Highways Authority expressed willingness to pay the solatium components from the date of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court passed in case of Tarsem Singh.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
26. However, in the light of legal principle laid down by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Rishabhkumar s/o. Babulal Jejani (Supra), grant of statutory amount and components are not permissible in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act."
8.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Incidentally, Rishabhkumar (supra) takes the view that whatever the Principal District Judge in a Petition under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act could not have done, the same cannot be done by the Appeal court under Section 37 of the Arbitration Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: In such circumstances, we cannot appreciate the NHAI's stance of raising the plea that these petitions should not be entertained because the Petitioners have an alternate remedy under Section 37 of the Arbitration Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 9. It is well settled that the rule of exhaustion of alternate remedies is a self-imposed restriction on exercising extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Before 903-WP.9608.2023 & 904.WP.11052.2024.DOCX applying this Rule, the court must see whether the alternate remedy is indeed efficacious.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: There is no point in relegating the Petitioners to the remedy under Section 37 of the Arbitration Act, when the relief they claim cannot be granted under such proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Accordingly, we reject the unfortunate contention that these Petitions should not be entertained because the Petitioners have an alternative remedy under Section 37 of the said Act.

sentences.text: In the case of M/s Godrej Sara Lee Ltd Vs The Excise and Taxation officer-cum-Assessing Authority and Ors.3,Civil Appeal no.5393 of 2010 decided on 1 February 2023, the Hon'ble Supreme Court interfered with the dismissal of the writ petition by the High Court because the petitioner had not availed the alternate remedy.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court noted that such dismissal was improper because the High Court failed to examine whether an exceptional case has been made out.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court also noted that mere availability of an alternative remedy of appeal or revision would not oust the jurisdiction of the High Court and render a writ petition 'not maintainable'.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: Where the controversy is purely legal one and it does not involve 2023 (384) ELT 8 (SC) 903-WP.9608.2023 & 904.WP.11052.2024.DOCX disputed questions of fact but only involves questions of law, then it should be decided by the High Court instead of dismissing the writ petition on the ground of an alternative remedy being available.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: 12. There is no serious dispute regarding the facts or applicable law in these matters.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The PDJ has held that the Petitioners are entitled to the benefits in terms of Tarsem Singh (Supra).
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The NHAI offered such benefits from the date of the judgment.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

sentences.text: The so- called alternative remedy is ineffective.
sentences._hearing_file: Ananda Revji Sanap vs Competent Authority And SpecialLand... on 9 May, 2025.json

In such circumstances, we cannot appreciate the NHAI's stance of raising the plea that these petitions should not be entertained because the Petitioners have an alternate remedy under Section 37 of the Arbitration Act.
9. It is well settled that the rule of exhaustion of alternate remedies is a self-imposed restriction on exercising extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
Before 903-WP.9608.2023 & 904.WP.11052.2024.DOCX applying this Rule, the court must see whether the alternate remedy is indeed efficacious.
There is no point in relegating the Petitioners to the remedy under Section 37 of the Arbitration Act, when the relief they claim cannot be granted under such proceedings.
If we were to relegate the Petitioners to the remedy of Section 37, the Appeal Court, being bound by the decision in Rishabhkumar (supra), would have no option but to dismiss such appeals by declining to modify the arbitral award.
Such a remedy can hardly be called an efficacious one.
In the case of M/s Godrej Sara Lee Ltd Vs The Excise and Taxation officer-cum-Assessing Authority and Ors.3,Civil Appeal no.5393 of 2010 decided on 1 February 2023, the Hon'ble Supreme Court interfered with the dismissal of the writ petition by the High Court because the petitioner had not availed the alternate remedy.
Where the controversy is purely legal one and it does not involve 2023 (384) ELT 8 (SC) 903-WP.9608.2023 & 904.WP.11052.2024.DOCX disputed questions of fact but only involves questions of law, then it should be decided by the High Court instead of dismissing the writ petition on the ground of an alternative remedy being available.
The PDJ has held that the Petitioners are entitled to the benefits in terms of Tarsem Singh (Supra).
The NHAI offered such benefits from the date of the judgment.
There is no benefit in relegating the Petitioners to avail themselves of such an alternative remedy,
thus depriving them of the benefits to which they are entitled.
Since the petitioners only claim statutory reliefs in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Tarsem Singh (supra), we see nothing wrong in their invoking the extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution.
